recipes.title: Misir Wat (Spiced Red Lentil Stew)
recipes.dish_alt: A mound of deep reddish-brown Misir Wat lentil stew served on injera, alongside greens
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Misir Wat on a Fasting Platter
recipes.prep_alt: Misir Wat shown as part of a full Ethiopian vegetarian fasting platter with cabbage, greens, and salad

sections.heading: Steps
items: Warm the oil (or niter kibbeh) in a pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook 8-10 minutes, stirring, until soft and golden.
Add the garlic and ginger and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the berbere and tomato paste, cooking 1-2 minutes until deep red and fragrant.
Rinse the lentils, then add them to the pot along with the stock or water. Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat and simmer, uncovered, 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the lentils are fully soft and the stew has thickened.
Season with salt to taste, thinning with a splash more water if needed.
Serve warm with injera, or over rice as a shortcut.

recipes.title: Tibs (Sautéed Beef with Peppers & Onions)
recipes.dish_alt: Sizzling strips of Tibs beef served in a traditional black clay pot
recipes.prep_alt: A clay pot of Tibs beef strips kept warm over a small charcoal stove

sections.heading: Ingredients by Serving
rows: Beef sirloin, cut into thin strips
Green bell pepper or jalapeño, sliced

sections.heading: Steps
items: Pat the beef strips dry and season with salt and pepper.
Heat the niter kibbeh (or butter) in a skillet over high heat until shimmering.
Sear the beef 2-3 minutes, tossing occasionally, until browned outside but still pink in the middle. Remove to a plate.
In the same skillet, add the onion and pepper, cooking 4-5 minutes until softened and lightly charred in spots.
Add the garlic, ginger, and rosemary (if using), cooking 1 minute until fragrant.
Stir in the berbere and a pinch of salt.
Return the beef and any juices to the skillet and toss 2-3 minutes until coated and cooked to your liking.
Serve hot, straight from the pan, with injera or flatbread.

recipes.title: Shiro Wat (Spiced Chickpea-Flour Stew)
recipes.dish_alt: A black bowl of smooth, reddish-orange Shiro Wat chickpea stew served with injera
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Shiro Wat Spooned onto Injera
recipes.prep_alt: A portion of Shiro Wat spooned onto a round of injera, ready to be shared

sections.heading: Steps
items: Heat the oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook 5 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the chopped tomato and berbere, cooking 2-3 minutes until the tomato breaks down and the mixture is deep red.
In a separate bowl, whisk the chickpea flour into the water until completely smooth with no lumps.
Pour the chickpea-flour mixture into the pot, whisking constantly as it heats to prevent clumping.
Bring to a gentle simmer and cook 8-10 minutes, stirring frequently, until thick, glossy, and no longer tastes raw or floury.
Season with salt, thin with a splash more water if needed, and serve hot with injera.

recipes.title: Atkilt Wat (Cabbage, Carrot & Potato Stew)
recipes.dish_alt: Turmeric-yellow Atkilt Wat with visible cabbage and carrot pieces served on injera
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Atkilt Wat on a Mixed Platter
recipes.prep_alt: Atkilt Wat plated alongside collard greens and other Ethiopian stews on injera

sections.heading: Steps
items: Heat the oil in a wide pan or pot over medium heat. Add the onion, garlic, and ginger, cooking 3-4 minutes until softened.
Stir in the turmeric and cumin, cooking 1 minute until fragrant and the onions are stained gold.
Add the potato and the water, cover, and cook 8-10 minutes until the potato is nearly tender.
Add the carrot, cover, and cook 5 minutes more.
Add the cabbage and salt, cover, and cook 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until tender but the cabbage still has a little bite.
Taste and adjust salt. Serve warm, on its own or alongside a wat.

recipes.title: Doro Wat (Spiced Chicken Stew)
recipes.dish_alt: A chicken drumstick and hard-boiled egg half in deep red Doro Wat sauce, served on injera
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Doro Wat Plated on a Full Platter
recipes.prep_alt: A formal serving of Doro Wat and other wats plated together atop injera

sections.heading: Steps
items: Melt the niter kibbeh (or butter) in a heavy pot over low heat. Add the red onion, cover, and cook 20-25 minutes, stirring every few minutes, until deeply softened and jammy.
Add the garlic and ginger, cooking 2-3 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in the berbere and tomato paste, cooking 2 minutes until the mixture turns deep brick red and smells toasted.
Add the chicken thighs, turning to coat every piece in the spiced onions.
Pour in the stock or water, bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook 25-30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the chicken is cooked through and tender.
Nestle the hard-boiled eggs into the sauce, spooning some sauce over each. Simmer uncovered 5-10 minutes so the eggs soak up flavor and the sauce thickens slightly.
Season with salt to taste. Serve hot with injera.

recipes.title: Key Wat (Spiced Beef Stew)
recipes.dish_alt: A bowl of deep red Key Wat beef stew topped with a slice of hard-boiled egg
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Key Wat on an Injera Platter
recipes.prep_alt: A beef-style wat plated within a mixed injera platter with lentils and greens

sections.heading: Steps
items: Heat the niter kibbeh (or oil) in a heavy pot or Dutch oven over medium heat. Season the beef with salt and pepper, then brown it in batches, 2-3 minutes per side. Remove to a plate.
In the same pot, add the onion and cook 12-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply golden and softened.
Add the garlic and ginger, cooking 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Stir in the berbere and tomato paste, cooking 2 minutes until deep red and fragrant.
Return the beef and any juices to the pot, then pour in the stock or water. Bring to a simmer.
Cover and simmer on low 35-40 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the beef is fork-tender.
Uncover and simmer 5 more minutes to thicken slightly if needed. Season with salt.
Serve hot with injera or rice.

recipes.title: Gomen (Collard Greens with Garlic & Ginger)
recipes.dish_alt: A pile of dark, glossy sautéed Gomen collard greens beside ayib cheese on injera
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Gomen on a Vegetarian Sampler
recipes.prep_alt: Gomen collard greens plated within a full Ethiopian vegetarian sampler platter

sections.heading: Steps
items: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, garlic, and ginger, cooking 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until deeply softened.
Add the collard greens in batches, stirring to wilt each addition before adding more.
Stir in the cumin (if using) and a splash of water or stock. Cover and simmer 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the greens are tender.
Season with salt to taste. Serve warm, on its own or alongside Doro Wat or Key Wat.

recipes.title: Injera (Teff Sourdough Flatbread) (Bonus)
recipes.dish_alt: A round of injera flatbread on a platter surrounded by eight kinds of stew
recipes.prep_label: Prep — Pouring Batter onto the Mitad
recipes.prep_alt: Injera batter being poured onto a hot traditional mitad griddle

sections.heading: Steps
items: Whisk the teff flour, all-purpose flour, yeast, and salt together in a large bowl.
Add the warm water and whisk until you have a smooth, thin, pourable batter — thinner than pancake batter.
Stir in the vinegar. Cover and let sit in a warm spot 45-60 minutes until bubbly on the surface (or refrigerate overnight for better flavor).
Just before cooking, whisk in the baking soda for a last burst of bubbles.
Heat a large nonstick skillet over medium heat and lightly oil it.
Pour a thin, even layer of batter into the pan, swirling to coat the bottom.
Cover and cook 2-3 minutes, undisturbed, until the surface is covered in small holes and the edges lift away from the pan. Do not flip.
Slide onto a plate to cool. Repeat with the remaining batter, stacking cooked injera between layers of parchment or a clean towel.
Serve at room temperature, torn into pieces, alongside the wats.
